Context/Background: Renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features (sRCC) is a highly aggressive tumor type yet preferentially responds to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). sRCC is unique in its ability to develop from various epithelial RCC subtypes, most frequently ccRCC, and sarcomatoid features typically exist as foci nested within an epithelioid RCC. Sarcomatoid clones are thought to arise from transformation of an epithelioid RCC cell through epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).To better understand microenvironmental mediators of the paradoxical immune sensitivity of sRCC, we performed single-cell analyses of human sRCC tumors compared against clear cell RCC (ccRCC), with validation spatially and in bulk transcriptomic datasets totaling over 3,000 RCC tumors.
Prompt: Gene expression counts were aggregated by case and differential expression analysis on pseudobulked counts was performed. Based on the differential gene expression results, run GSEA on hallmark genesets, and provide a brief discussion of pathways important in the sRCC vs ccRCC context. From the top 20 differentially expressed genes, prioritize 5 genes and discuss their possible roles in tumorigenesis and sarcomatoid transformation.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
In this analysis of pseudobulked single-cell RNA-seq from human renal cell carcinoma, differential expression between sarcomatoid RCC (sRCC) and clear cell RCC (ccRCC) was performed per case. 14,871 genes were tested; the top 20 by FDR (2 × 10⁻⁷ to 3.87 × 10⁻²) include SEMA3C, DCBLD2, EPO, TFAP2A, TRNP1, NPR1, HRH2, MOXD1, PLTP, CAPN6, COL6A1, AKR1B1, CHST15, TEAD2, BIRC7, CASK, ZCCHC24, CD44, PTPRH, and PLAU. GSEA on the MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 collection identified 13 enriched pathways (p < 0.05, FDR < 0.05), most notably Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition, Myogenesis, KRAS Signaling (down‐regulated gene set), Coagulation, Apical Surface, and Apical Junction (all up in sRCC), versus Interferon-Alpha Response, TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB, PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling, and Androgen Response (down in sRCC).  

Keywords  
• EMT  
• Tumor Microenvironment  
• Immunomodulation  
• ECM remodeling  
• Sarcomatoid Transformation  

Candidate Genes  
• SEMA3C  
• DCBLD2  
• TFAP2A  
• CD44  
• PLAU  

Pathway Enrichments  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 9 up, 4 down (total 13) → 69.2% up, 30.8% down (ratio = 2.25)

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme                      | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                                    |
|----------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition | Up        | MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, COL12A1, BGN, …, CD44, TNC, FN1, COL1A2 |
| Myogenesis                 | Up        | TNNT1, PVALB, NOS1, FGF2, MYLK, COL6A3, COL1A1, IGF1, SPARC |
| KRAS Signaling Dn          | Up        | NOS1, PCDHB1, THRB, IGFBP2, TGFB2, CCNA1                     |
| Coagulation                | Up        | PLAT, CAPN2, PLG, SH2B2, CFH, PLAU, MMP1, TIMP1, FN1         |
| Apical Surface             | Up        | SHROOM2, EFNA5, PLAUR, DC***LD2, GAS1                        |
| Apical Junction            | Up        | NEXN, SHROOM2, ITGB4, CLDN7, MMP2, VCL, CDH1, ITGB1          |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme                              | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                           |
|------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|
| Interferon Alpha Response          | Down      | TRIM21, HERC6, ISG15, BATF2, PSMB9, CXCL10         |
| TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB          | Down      | NFKBIA, TRAF1, SGK1, VEGFA, JUN, CCL4, ICAM1       |
| PI3K/AKT/mTOR Signaling            | Down      | AKT1, CDK4, RAC1, MAPK1, EGFR, CDKN1A              |
| Androgen Response                  | Down      | AKT1, SGK1, NKX3-1, CCND1, B2M                     |

Discussion of Global Patterns  
sRCC cells exhibit a robust EMT signature (NES 5.34, FDR 4.6 × 10⁻⁶), consistent with epithelioid-to-mesenchymal transformation. Upregulation of Myogenesis and apical junction/surface modules suggests reprogramming of cytoskeletal‐ECM interfaces. Coagulation pathway enrichment may reflect stromal or endothelial recruitment in the sarcomatoid microenvironment. Downregulation of Interferon-α and TNF-α/NF-κB pathways—typically linked to innate immunity—may paradoxically accompany increased immune checkpoint sensitivity in sRCC. Suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR and Androgen Response further delineates altered growth and hormone-related signaling.

Targeted (Keyword-Guided) Subset  
Filtering for “Epithelial” from the full GSEA results recapitulates only the EMT term (NES 5.34, FDR 4.6 × 10⁻⁶), underscoring its singular prominence among epithelial-related modules. No other hallmark terms directly reference “Mesenchymal” or “Sarcomatoid” by name.

Key Genes/Proteins (Leading Edge)  
| Gene   | Direction | Role/Function                                      | Pathway(s)                         |
|--------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| CD44   | Up        | Hyaluronan receptor; EMT, migration, stemness      | EMT                                |
| PLAU   | Up        | Urokinase plasminogen activator; ECM degradation  | Coagulation, KRAS Dn, Apical Surface |
| SEMA3C | Up        | Axon guidance cue; cell motility, angiogenesis     | Apical Surface, Apical Junction    |
| DCBLD2 | Up        | Endothelial receptor; cell adhesion, migration     | Apical Surface                     |
| TFAP2A | Up        | Transcription factor AP-2α; epithelial differentiation | KRAS Dn                            |

Comparisons  
- EMT and ECM remodeling upregulation is shared with other mesenchymal‐transition contexts, notably in lung and breast cancers, suggesting a conserved transformation module.  
- Downregulation of interferon/NF-κB contrasts with canonical immune-cold profiles, highlighting a unique sRCC immune-sensitive state.  

Implications  
The pronounced EMT program and ECM remodeling in sRCC may underpin both aggressive invasion and neoantigen exposure, contributing to paradoxical ICB responsiveness. Targeting ECM components (e.g., CD44 or PLAU) could modulate tumor stroma and potentiate checkpoint blockade.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate protein-level expression of SEMA3C and DCBLD2 in sarcomatoid foci via immunohistochemistry.  
2. Correlate leading-edge CD44 and PLAU expression with ICB response status in bulk cohorts.  
3. Assess functional impact of TFAP2A knockdown on EMT markers in ccRCC cell lines.  
4. Determine whether downregulated interferon/NF-κB signatures reflect intrinsic tumor cell suppression or microenvironmental modulation.

References  
None available (no PMIDs/PMCIDs were retrieved via leading-edge or literature tool calls).
